summary: For bounded gonality and sufficiently large prime level, every curve on the diagonal modular quotient lies on a cyclic Hecke locus. The roadmap combines compact hyperbolic geometry, arithmetic repulsion and ramification estimates, and then proves the linear-torsion descent bridge for nonisotrivial elliptic families over every algebraically closed characteristic-zero field.

nodes.title: Projective p-frames and their two components
nodes.statement: For a prime p>3 over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, form the projective-frame coarse curve Y(p) from the existing full-level curve by identifying bases φ:F_p²≃E[p] under φ↦aφ for a∈F_p×. Let X(p) be its imported smooth proper compactification. The Weil-pairing value on a basis, modulo squares, labels exactly two geometric connected components. G=PGL₂(F_p) acts by g·(E,[φ])=(E,[φ∘g⁻¹]); its component-preserving subgroup is PSL₂(F_p). The construction uses existing level moduli, rather than a new elliptic-curve or compactification object.
proofSteps: Apply the full-level and coarse-space interfaces, including boundary p-gons, then take the finite scalar quotient. Scalar change squares the determinant pairing; the two square classes account for the components by the imported connectedness theorem.
Descend the GL₂ right action with the inverse so that it is a left G-action. Compare a chosen fixed-pairing component with the usual Γ(p) quotient, accounting for the central ±I.

Transport all algebraic maps through characteristic-zero base change; complex conjugation transports the pairing and its component label. Projective framing retains the automorphism [-1], so this coarse space is not a fine moduli space with a universal elliptic scheme.
acceptance: Check the stated hypotheses and constants; preserve component and map-degree conventions in every use.

nodes.title: The diagonal quotient surface
nodes.statement: Let S=X(p)×X(p) and Z(p)=S/G for the diagonal projective-frame action. This is a normal projective coarse surface, finite below S. Its smooth-level geometric points classify (E₁,E₂,[ψ]) with ψ:E₁[p]≃E₂[p] up to common scalar. The square class of det ψ labels its two components. For each determinant square class choose a fixed-pairing component presentation by a diagonal, possibly conjugated, PSL₂ action; changing the auxiliary nonsquare gives an equivariantly isomorphic presentation.
proofSteps: Apply the finite quotient universal property to S, using a norm of an ample line bundle to supply an invariant projective embedding.
Composition φ₂φ₁⁻¹ is invariant under simultaneous framing change. Conversely two framed presentations of the same triple differ by a diagonal element of G.

Reduce each G-orbit to a selected first component. Its stabilizer is PSL₂, while the second component records the determinant square class; a chosen nonsquare identifies that component with the first and conjugates its action. Prove independence before using the erratum’s fixed-pairing notation.

nodes.title: Heegner and anti-Heegner CM strata
nodes.statement: A smooth-level pair (x,y) belongs to CM only when its two projective point stabilizers share a nonidentity element. Choose corresponding nontrivial automorphisms of E_x,E_y with matching characteristic polynomial, allowing a simultaneous sign adjustment. Put the pair in CM⁺ when their tangent eigenvalues agree and in CM⁻ when they are conjugate unequal eigenvalues. This definition is independent of the common generator, compatible lifts and projective frame representatives. Equal j-invariants alone do not define CM.
proofSteps: Use the faithful derivative character of the effective cyclic stabilizer of order 2 or 3. Changing the common generator applies the same power to both eigenvalues, preserving agreement versus opposition.
Check the order-3 lifts using t²+t+I=0, and the order-4 lift using t²=−I. These are different polynomials.

Conjugating the second complex structure interchanges CM⁺ and CM⁻; simultaneous G action preserves each. Over another characteristic-zero algebraically closed field formulate the same distinction by the algebraic tangent character, transporting through an embedding only for the metric.

nodes.title: Cyclic Hecke loci and weighted pull-push
nodes.statement: For m≥1 with p∤m, use the existing cyclic-isogeny correspondence on X(p) to define T_m⊂S by [φ₂]=[f[p]φ₁] for a cyclic degree-m isogeny f. Let H_m be its finite image in Z; a Hecke curve is an irreducible component of H_m. On normalized correspondences with projections a,b define T_m* C=(id×a)_*(id×b)^*C as an effective one-cycle, including generic map degrees. Each projection degree is ψ(m)=m∏_{ℓ|m}(1+1/ℓ), so Deg(T_m*C)=ψ(m)Deg(C) and ψ(m)≪m². These are applications of R14.1, not a second general correspondence construction.
proofSteps: Restrict R14.1 to cyclic prime-to-p isogenies and projective-frame quotients. Count cyclic order-m subgroups by prime powers and multiply; distinguish them from all order-m subgroups.
At the boundary use R13.1/R13.3 p-gons and the maps (t,a)↦(t^m,a mod p) from the pm-gon and (t,a)↦(t^d,a) on the p-gon. The component-group source of the first map is Z/(pm).

Apply flat pullback and proper pushforward with projection formula; symmetry of correspondence degrees gives the canonical-degree identity. All maps preserve scalar independence, transport determinant components by the isogeny multiplier, and commute with conjugation and characteristic-zero base change.

nodes.title: Compact triangle uniformization
nodes.statement: For prime p>5, the orbifold with underlying X(1) and cone orders (2,3,p) is uniformized by the orientation-preserving hyperbolic triangle group Δ(2,3,p). Its deck group is PSL₂(F_p); obtain the other component by the projective-frame transport. The cusped quotient Γ(p)\H and compact quotient Ξ(p)\H have distinct universal covers/maps.
proofSteps: Use Fuchsian polygon and orbifold-covering theory for angles π/2,π/3,π/p, whose sum is <π exactly when p>6.
Identify the compactification map on orbifold fundamental groups: kill the pth power of a peripheral generator. Its normal closure is contained in Γ(p), yielding the finite deck quotient.
Use R12.3/R13.4b for the algebraic compactification and ComplexComparisonPartII for comparison; prove torsion-freeness of Ξ from the actual level cover and its local ramification.

nodes.title: A systolic witness surviving cusp filling
nodes.statement: For sufficiently large prime p write p=3r+x with x∈{1,2}. The integral matrix M_p=[[1+xp,3p],[p(2−x²+2px)/3,1+2p²−xp]] belongs to Γ(p), has trace 2p²+2, and its image under the compact triangle representation has absolute trace (27/(4π²))p²+O(p). Thus its image in Ξ(p) is hyperbolic and nonidentity. Its cusped and compact geodesic lengths are both 4 log p+O(1), giving the required upper bounds for geodesics nontrivial after cusp filling.
proofSteps: Verify integrality, determinant one and reduction to I. With U(t)=[[1,t],[0,1]] and L(t)=[[1,0],[t,1]], factor M_p=−L(2r)U(3)L(−r−1)U(3) if x=1; if x=2 use L(2r+1)U(−3)L(−r−1)U(1)L(1)U(1). These are exact integer identities.

Substitute U_p,L_p into each word. The two large lower powers divided by p converge to ±(√3/(2π))N with N=[[0,0],[1,0]], and have bounded remainder. The fixed-power words converge to U(±3), or U(1)L(1)U(1). The leading traces in both cases are 27/(4π²).
The triangle length formula 2 arcosh(|tr|/2) proves nontriviality in the compact group and the length asymptotics. This replaces the published witness U(p)L(−p), which is killed by cusp filling.
acceptance: Check the two exact word identities and the positive leading trace separately for p≡1 and p≡2 mod 3.
Check p=7 and 11 as integer examples; asymptotics alone do not specify an explicit numerical final threshold.

For a shortest compact geodesic γ of length L≤4 log p+C, use disjoint embedded cusp discs of radii R_b=(1/2)log p and inner radii R_s=(1/4)log p. Every connected visit to an outer disc reaching its inner disc costs at least 2(R_b−R_s), so there are O(1) deep visits, counting repeated visits to the same cusp.

Outside the inner discs, the metric comparison costs O(e^{−R_s}L)=o(1). For each deep arc lift to its embedded hyperbolic disc, use cosh r(s)=cosh r_min cosh(s−s₀), and integrate coth(r(s)/2)−1 on r≥1 to obtain a uniform O(1) error. Replace any r<1 part by a unit-circle arc; its cusped length is O(1) by the metric comparison.

The resulting loop in Y is homotopic to γ in X and has cusped length ≤L+O(1). It is neither contractible nor peripheral in Y because its filled class is nontrivial. Apply the cusped lower bound. The argument counts visits and does not use the source’s unsupported at-most-one-cusp assertion.

nodes.title: Small equations reconstruct a signed Hecke locus
nodes.statement: Fix A. A unique invertible projective 2×2 solution over F_p of integral linear equations with coefficients bounded by p^(Aδ) has a primitive integral representative Q of height p^(O_A(δ)), for sufficiently small δ and large p. Put m=|det Q|; then p∤m. If det Q>0 its Smith form gives a cyclic degree-m holomorphic isogeny; if det Q<0, composition with the fixed real reflection gives the corresponding conjugate Hecke locus after complex realization. On cusp data the two cases give the respective ordinary or conjugate Hecke boundary incidence. Uniqueness does not determine the sign, and multiplication by −1 cannot change it.
proofSteps: Uniqueness of an invertible projective solution forces a one-dimensional kernel for p>3: in a projective line of matrices the determinant is a quadratic, so an invertible point would give at least p−1 invertible projective points. Thus the modular rank is three. A nonzero rank-three minor and its cofactors give the kernel vector. All relevant rank-four minors are bounded by p^(O_A(δ))<p, so their vanishing modulo p implies vanishing over Z; the same rational kernel is one-dimensional. The cofactor vector is nonzero modulo p and has the required height.

Divide out the gcd; reduction is still the same invertible projective matrix, so p∤det Q. Keep the sign. Positive determinant is automatic only in the definite CM centralizer application. For negative determinant factor Q as a positive-determinant matrix times the integral reflection diag(1,−1).

Use Smith normal form for the primitive positive lattice map. For a negative map use the conjugate complex structure and R12.6, then the same positive Smith form. Check the p-gon toric and component factors separately at the boundary; the sign is the ordinary versus conjugate Hecke distinction.

nodes.title: Quadratic centralizers give only logarithmically many small elements
nodes.statement: For a nonscalar rational 2×2 matrix N whose algebra Q[N] is reduced, the determinant-one integral elements in its centralizer with entrywise height ≤p^A have O_A(log p) possibilities, uniformly in N and its embedding. A nonreduced quadratic algebra is the unipotent case and must be returned to the cusp branch. Scalar common centralizers impose no rigidity and must be eliminated by additional intertwining equations.
proofSteps: In the imaginary quadratic case integral norm-one eigenvalues are roots of unity, leaving an absolute bound. In the split rational case they are rational algebraic integer units, hence ±1.

In the real quadratic case log of the absolute first eigenvalue embeds the norm-one unit group modulo a finite kernel into R. The trace of a nontrivial positive unit is an integer ≥3, giving a uniform positive separation for the logarithms. An eigenvalue has absolute value ≤2h(M), so only O_A(log p) separated values occur.
If the minimal polynomial has a repeated root, isolate its nilpotent part and its rational fixed line; this is the cusp/unipotent configuration, where the logarithmic count is not claimed.

For a fixed pair of projected bicusp centres a₁,a₂ in the cusp-branch decomposition, the transformations carrying a₂ to a₁ form one order-p stabilizer coset. The short-displacement comparison can be made in either slot separately, by taking inverses; use the farther of that slot’s two cusp coordinates, so d=d_S(z_i,a_i). With R=O(δρ_X), this gives O(1+p^{1+Aδ}e^{−d}) for d≥1 and O(p) for d<1. At d=0 use p directly. The weaker shell bound with an exponential O(δρ_X) loss is sufficient for diagonal multiplicity.
proofSteps: Attach the two projected bicusp centres from the cusp-branch lift. The deck transformation sends the source centre to the target centre. Fixing a pair leaves a coset of the source stabilizer, of order p. Two short transformations in this coset differ by a rotation with O(δρ_X) displacement. Apply this to the source slot and, by inversion, to the target slot. The radius R₀+O(δρ_X)<ρ_X ensures the short lifts agree.
For a rotation through 2πk/p in an embedded hyperbolic disc, compute sinh(distance(z,g^kz)/2)=sinh(d)|sin(πk/p)|.
Count the equally spaced angles satisfying this inequality and include the identity by the additive 1. The two coordinate inequalities only reduce the count.

The existing compactified level moduli object, finite scalar quotient compatibility and properness over the j-line.
Tate and boundary charts, the correct p-/pm-gon component groups, finite inertia and the maps used to extend cyclic Hecke correspondences through cusps.
The existing projective coarse modular curve/surface comparisons and classifying maps. Quotienting projective frames leaves [-1] inertia; a fine universal family is not inferred.
The existing generic compactification/uniformization comparison identifying the filled orbifold-cover quotient with the supplied algebraic X(p).

The existing normalized cyclic prime-to-p isogeny correspondence, its two finite projections, boundary extension and base change. Export the cyclic degree ψ(m), not σ₁(m), and its projection formula. This roadmap adds only proof-specific restrictions and estimates.

Finite quotients of normal projective characteristic-zero varieties by a finite group: existence as a projective scheme, orbit fibres, quotient universal property, invariant norm polarization, finite map, étaleness on the free locus and characteristic-zero base change. Include S_n quotients of projective surfaces and the relative cycle/norm morphism for finite flat degree-n families. Existing SF.1 nodes provide algebraic spaces, not this complete projective quotient/cycle theorem.

In the named setting of projective characteristic-zero surfaces: resolve cyclic quotient charts 1/n(1,a), with Hirzebruch–Jung chains, rational exceptional components and strict transforms; provide Castelnuovo contraction of smooth rational (−1)-curves to smooth projective surfaces and termination by decreasing Picard number. Also supply smooth connected sufficiently ample surface sections for the Proposition27 check. These are precise requests to the existing birational-geometry stage, with a dedicated surface-contraction Part II proposed in restructure; no existing node is claimed to supply them.

Intersection degree, finite flat pullback and proper cycle pushforward with generic-degree multiplicities, projection formula, canonical products; self-intersection of quotient-resolution chains and the update C_new²=C_old²+(C_old·E)² under contraction of a smooth rational (−1)-curve. The contraction theorem itself is a separately proposed extension.

Smooth proper models of one-variable function fields over an algebraically closed field, finite normalization, extension/factorization of maps from smooth curves to proper targets, normalization-genus invariance and their analytic comparison contracts. This imports the curve objects and does not replan their divisor or Riemann–Roch theory.

Effective PSL/PGL Möbius actions, faithful real disc/half-plane comparison, and central scalar conventions used by the marked triangle action.

Finite stabilizers of a Fuchsian action are cyclic; local quotient charts have z↦z^e; an effective finite group fixing a smooth curve point injects into its tangent character. Supply the elliptic/cusp inertia comparison for the modular cover.

Hyperbolic polygon and triangle-group uniformization with angle-sum criterion; translation length 2 arcosh(|tr|/2); distance/cosine identities; orbifold Gauss–Bonnet Area=π[PSL₂(Z):Γ]/3 for the cusped congruence quotient.

The compactified quotient Riemann surface, torsion-free compact uniformizing group and finite branched-cover Euler characteristic; compare complex compactification and modular boundary ramification.
Finite holomorphic-map degree, multiplicity and the exact Riemann–Hurwitz formula on compact Riemann surfaces, consistent with the algebraic curve dictionary.

Effective descent and finite-presentation spread of elliptic schemes, homomorphisms, full level/torsion isomorphisms, maps and pencils to finitely generated subfields; preserve smoothness, connectedness and the inverse identities after shrinking.
